:JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.8,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.
2.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 21022019 at about 7.00 p.m. when the Petitioner after having tea in the Green park Hotel situated in front of A.C. Office at Pandavapura and stood on the edge of the road to cross TumkurMysore road, at that time, a Hero Honda bearing Regn.KA09ES3649 ridden by its rider came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Pandavapura Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to KIMS hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as a contractor cum agriculturist and earning Rs.50,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries which caused permanent disablement.
The Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 and 2 had appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed their Objection statement to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.1, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the offending Hero Honda by its rider.
Further, it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further, it contended that the Petitioner himself is the cause of the said accident.
The rider of the offending motor cycle did not possess valid and effective driving licence to ride the motor cycle.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

A.S.Nanjappa vs United India Insurance on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147659217/
2

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2, he denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the offending Hero Honda by its rider.
Further, he has contended that the accident occurred due to negligence of Petitioner.
Further, he has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further, he stated that the motor cycle is duly insured with the Respondent No.1.
Hence, he is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Hence,
among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my Learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 21.02.2019 at about 7.00 p.m. on PandavapuraMysore main road, in front of A.C.Office, near Green Park Hotel, Pandavapura Town, Mandya District, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent riding of the Motor Cycle bearing Regn.KA09ES3649?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3. What Order or Award ?
5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 6 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.6.
He also examined a witness as P.W.2 and got marked 6 documents as per Ex.P7 to P12 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondents did not choose to lead any evidence.

6. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 7. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 21022019 at about 7.00 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Hero Honda bearing Regn.KA09ES3649.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending two wheeler.

A.S.Nanjappa vs United India Insurance on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147659217/
3 9
. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and he also examined one witness as P.W.2 and got marked total 12 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P12.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot Panchanama, Wound certificate and Charge sheet.
Ex.P.5 is the Medical bills and Ex.P.6 is the Prescriptions.

10. Upon going through Ex.P1, it shows that on the complaint lodged by the Complainant by name Nanjappa before Pandavapura Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the rider of the Hero Honda bearing Reg.KA09ES3649 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P2 is the Spot Panchanama which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P3 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P4 is the copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Pandavapura Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the rider of the offending Hero Honda for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
11.

Upon going through the Chargesheet i.e., Ex.P4 Column No.17 reads as under:
" 21022019   700       .    1         12     09 3649                  1     1      ,
 , ,     
 .
12. Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.Ravish as P.W.2 and he also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
13. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 has cross examined the P.W.1.
But, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the Petitioner.
14. The Respondents did not choose to lead evidence to substantiate their Objection statement contentions.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the depositions and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'Affirmative'.

15. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending Hero Honda by its rider, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

A.S.Nanjappa vs United India Insurance on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147659217/
4 16.
In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 63 years.
He has not produced any document for age proof.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident to be taken at 63 years for the purpose of assessment.
17. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as Contractor cum Agriculturist and earning Rs.50,000/ per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to prove his income.

Therefore, in the absence of actual proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.14,000/p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2019, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
19.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P3 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Swelling and tenderness over distal 1/3rd of right leg.
2. Abrasion wound over left great toe.
3. Abrasion wound over nasal bridge.
4. Sutured wound over right fore head.
Xray shows Communited fracture distal shaft of tibia and fibula of right leg.
Further, the Doctor has opined that Injuries No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 to 4 are simple in injuries.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
20.

Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the problems he facing due to the accidental injuries, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/
under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
21.

The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 22.02.2019 to 10.03.2019 at Kempegowda Institute of Medical Science Hospital and A.S.Nanjappa vs United India Insurance on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147659217/
5 Research Center, Bangalore i.e., for 19 days.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further, P.W.2 Dr.Ravish has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
Upon going through Ex.P.7 i.e., Case sheet supports the evidence of PW.1.
Therefore, the total laid up period of PW.1 to be taken as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,000/ (Rs.14,000/ per month) under this head.

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
22.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period,
the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
23. The Petitioner has deposed that he spent Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 83 medical bills along with advance receipts i.e., Ex.P.5 totally amounting to Rs.1,10,535/.
The advance bills are amounting to Rs.67,685/.
The Petitioner has not produced the Final bill.
I have gone through the medical bills.
The acceptable bills are amounting to Rs.1,10,535/.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,10,600/ as a compensation under this head.

VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
24.

The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not in a position to carry out the contract work and scar remains in the body which causes social stigma
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.
Further, the Petitioner got examined Dr.Ravish.V.N as P.W.2.
PW.2 has also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Further, he got marked Case sheet, X rays, OPD card and Disability Assessment Certificate at Ex.P.7 to P.12.
He assessed permanent physical disability at 36.06% to the right lower limb and disability to the whole body at 12.02%.
In the crossexamination he deposed that he has given treatment to the Petitioner.
He also deposed that Petitioner has taken follow up treatment in their hospital.
He admitted that the fracture of the Petitioner is united.
The implants are in situ.
He has denied the other suggestions putforth to him by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1.

A.S.Nanjappa vs United India Insurance on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147659217/
6

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 7.

With multiplier of 7, income of Rs.14,000/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.1,17,600/ (Rs.14,000/ x 12 =
1,68,000/, Rs.1,68,000/x 7 x 10/100 = 1,17,600/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,17,600/ under this head.

COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
28.
The doctor i.e., PW.2 has deposed that the Petitioner requires removal of implants which approximately cost about 30,000/ to 35,000/.
But, there is no estimation in this regard.
Hence, by considering the future medical expenses for removal of implants, it would be proper to grant Rs.10,000/ as a compensation under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
25.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs.1,10,600/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 28,000/ laid up period 6.

Future loss of income Rs.1,17,600/
7.
Future Medical expenses Rs. 10,000/ Total Rs.3,49,200/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,49,200/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

26. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing KA09ES 3649.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, Respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".

A.S.Nanjappa vs United India Insurance on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147659217/
7 27.
Point No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.3,49,200/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after his proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

Medical expenses Rs.1,10,600/

Future loss of income Rs.1,17,600/

Future Medical expenses Rs. 10,000/ Total Rs.3,49,200/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,49,200/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
Therefore, Respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
Point No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.3,49,200/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after his proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
